top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, independently reproduced invention in the sense of the Nobel will: the magic-wavelength lattice plus the 10^-18 strontium realisation enlarged what physics can measure, and the two-name allocation maps cleanly onto proposal and realisation with no omission inside the credited set. Topological insulators come second on maturity but their three-name allocation understates Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Moore-Balents and Hasan, and magic-angle graphene is still young with an unsettled mechanism and a contested third name. No award is the least preferred since a defensible, mature candidate exists.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented connection to the lattice-clock, topological-insulator or twisted-graphene candidates
